subject: Post-call: CityHealth security posture & private deployment options
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@cityhealth.org>, Dr. Emily Rhodes <emily.rhodes@cityhealth.org>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: CityHealth security posture & private deployment options

Hi Alex / Emily —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the security/compliance questions you raised for a private deployment of Redwood: 

Recap of asks from CityHealth:
- SOC 2 status and typical evidence artifacts you need for procurement (attestations, control mappings)
- GDPR/HIPAA applicability and our standard safeguards for PHI in private deployments
- Vendor security questionnaire — you mentioned a spreadsheet in procurement
- Network isolation options: VPC peering, customer-managed NAT/Firewall, and an air-gap/appliance path
- A simple deployment sketch showing control plane vs data plane boundaries and where logs/evidence will live

What I can commit to from our side: 
1) I’ll send our SOC 2 Type II summary and control map (redacted) by EOD Wednesday.
2) Marissa (CS) will start the vendor questionnaire intake and pull in our security lead for any detailed answers.
3) Neha will draft a deployment sketch showing the private control plane option + an on-prem appliance flow for your compliance team to review.

Immediate asks for you: 
- Can procurement share the vendor questionnaire spreadsheet (we can pre-fill) and a preferred evidence upload method?
- For the air-gapped option, can you confirm whether CityHealth would prefer: a) temporary physical media transfer for model weights/evidence, or b) an on-prem appliance with no external egress?

Next sync: I’m proposing a 30-min follow-up on Thursday to review the completed questionnaire and the sketch. I’ve proposed slots in the calendar invite I’ll send after this email.

Attachments: I’ll attach the questionnaire template we prefer (we can accept yours) and a rough sketch template.

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0189

From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@cityhealth.org>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Dr. Emily Rhodes <emily.rhodes@cityhealth.org>, procurement@cityhealth.org
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: CityHealth security posture & private deployment options

Markus —

Appreciate the rapid recap. A few quick notes from procurement and security so we can prep: 

1) SOC 2: we require an active SOC 2 Type II with a report covering the most recent 12-month period. If you can share the executive summary + control mapping (System Description -> Controls) that will get us started. Full report via an NDA is fine.
2) HIPAA: CityHealth will treat any PHI as regulated. We need confirmation that in a private deployment PHI never leaves City-controlled networks unless explicitly allowed and logged.
3) Questionnaire: attaching the procurement spreadsheet (proc_vendor_questionnaire_vCityHealth.xlsx). Please pre-fill any fields you can and indicate where evidence links will be. We prefer a secure SFTP or a signed DocuSign upload link for artifacts.
4) Air-gap: the preference is an on-prem virtual appliance with no outbound internet allowed (option b). Physical media transfer is allowed only for initial seed data under strict chain-of-custody rules.

We have a compliance review window next week (Mon-Wed). If you can get the draft answers and the sketch in by end of day Friday it will allow us to include you in the review.

Thanks,
Alex
Senior Procurement Manager — CityHealth Network
alex.nguyen@cityhealth.org

Attachment: proc_vendor_questionnaire_vCityHealth.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: CityHealth security posture & private deployment options

Markus / team —

I’ve pulled the procurement spreadsheet Alex attached and started a row-by-row intake. Plan:
- I’ll pre-fill the administrative and process questions today (org charts, policy links, etc.).
- Neha — can you take the technical and deployment sketch? I started a draft in the shared Drive (link below).
- Vanessa — please loop in security@redwood so we can link the SOC 2 summary and identify any control gaps. We may need a one-hour async review with their lead for cryptography and key management specifics (CityHealth will likely want KMS/HSM attestation).

Proposed owner map: Marissa (questionnaire), Neha (deployment sketch & network isolation answers), Vanessa (evidence collection & audit artifacts).

Shared draft link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/CityHealth-intake-draft

I’ll drop the partially-complete spreadsheet back to Alex with notes for any items that need legal/security redlines.

Marissa
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@cityhealth.org>, Dr. Emily Rhodes <emily.rhodes@cityhealth.org>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 14:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: CityHealth security posture & private deployment options

Alex / Emily — quick update and confirming the next steps/timeline.

What we’re delivering by Friday EOD (15 Sep):
- SOC 2 Type II executive summary + control map (redacted).
- Completed vendor spreadsheet with inline notes for any items requiring legal input.
- Neha’s deployment sketch in PDF showing three variants: Private VPC (customer VPC peering + strict egress rules), Dedicated on-prem appliance (no egress), and Hybrid (control plane in customer VPC, data-plane isolated). The sketch will label where logs, audit artifacts, and KMS live.
- A checklist of evidence artifacts (e.g., key rotation logs, access reviews, trace samples) and suggested upload method (we recommend signed DocuSign bundle or SFTP to your procurement bucket).

Scheduling: I’ve proposed two 30-minute slots on Thursday in the calendar invite. If you need an earlier slot for the compliance review window, we can shift one of the slots to Wednesday afternoon.

Questions for you before we finalize the sketch: 
1) Is CityHealth comfortable with a customer-managed KMS in-cloud (you control keys) or do you require HSM-backed, on-prem KMS?
2) For the appliance option, will CityHealth require an air-gap acceptance test and evidence of no outbound packets during the operational window? We can run a test plan and provide packet captures and audit logs.

If it helps, we can also prepare a brief (1-page) mapping that shows how Redwood’s controls map to CityHealth’s procurement checklist — happy to prioritize that.

Thanks — looking forward to the review.

Regards,
Markus
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0189
